HISTORY & PHYSICAL (Super-Detailed)

Consult Summary:
48-year-old man with asthma presents with a 3-day history of frequent watery diarrhoea, central abdominal cramps, and one episode of vomiting; no blood noted. Clinical picture most consistent with acute infectious gastroenteritis; advised oral rehydration and to seek in-person review if symptoms worsen.

History:
• Presenting complaint: “Diarrhoea” for 3 days.  
• Onset/Timeline: Began abruptly 3 days ago; frequency unchanged (not better, not worse).  
• Character: Watery stools every ~10 minutes; urge to return to toilet immediately after defecation.  
• Associated abdominal pain: Central/peri-umbilical, mild-to-moderate, improves after bowel motion; mild tenderness on self-palpation.  
• Vomiting: Single episode this morning after eating fruit; no haematemesis (red colour thought to be strawberries).  
• Nausea: Intermittent.  
• Hydration/Nutrition: Reports limited oral intake and likely inadequate fluid intake.  
• Fever: Denies definite fever; mild sweating past 4 days, unsure of temperature.  
• Other ROS: No blood per rectum, no chest pain, baseline asthma-related breathlessness only, able to walk and talk, no dyspnoea beyond normal, no weight loss reported.  
• Exacerbating/Relieving factors: Pain improves after bowel movement; no clear dietary trigger identified.  
• Systems review: No urinary, neurological, or dermatological symptoms mentioned; no trauma.

Past Medical History:
• Asthma – controlled with inhaler (brand recently changed).  
• No other chronic illnesses reported.

Medications:
• Inhaler for asthma – dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
• NKDA (patient stated “I have NKDA allergy”).

Social History:
• Employment: Working but currently at home due to symptoms.  
• Anxiety noted; increased inhaler use with anxiety episodes.  
• Smoking, alcohol, recreational drugs: Not discussed.  
• Lives abroad (“foreigner”); financial/lifestyle factors not discussed.

Family History:
• Father died of colorectal (bowel) cancer ~10 years ago.

Physical Examination: (remote/video; limited)
• Vitals: Not provided.  
• General appearance: Able to converse; no respiratory distress described.  
• Abdomen: Patient-reported mild central tenderness; no radiation; no peritonism reported.  
• Cardiovascular/Respiratory/Neuro: No concerns voiced.

Investigations:
• None performed or available.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1 – Acute infectious gastroenteritis (likely viral)  
  • Assessment: Classic triad of abrupt watery diarrhoea, mild central cramps, and brief vomiting; no blood, severe pain, or systemic toxicity. DDx supports high likelihood.  
  • Plan:  
    – Advise aggressive oral hydration (water, oral rehydration salts if available).  
    – Encourage small, bland meals as tolerated; avoid dairy/irritants temporarily.  
    – Monitor for red flags: fever, persistent vomiting, blood in stool, worsening pain, signs of dehydration.  
    – Avoid empiric antibiotics at this stage (may worsen course).  
    – Stay home from work until symptoms improve (infection control, rest).  
    – Follow-up: If no improvement or deterioration within 24-48 h, arrange in-person GP assessment for physical exam, possible stool cultures, bloodwork, hydration status.  

Issue 2 – Dehydration risk  
  • Assessment: High stool frequency, limited fluid intake.  
  • Plan: Reinforce fluid targets; consider oral rehydration solution; educate on signs of dehydration (dizziness, reduced urine output).  

Issue 3 – Colorectal cancer anxiety / family history  
  • Assessment: Acute presentation not suggestive of malignancy, but positive first-degree family history (father).  
  • Plan: Reassured patient; advised formal discussion with GP once acute illness resolves regarding age-appropriate colorectal cancer screening (e.g., FIT testing or colonoscopy per local guidelines).

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Acute viral gastroenteritis – High likelihood: sudden onset, watery stools, mild cramps, self-limiting course, minimal systemic features.  
2. Bacterial food-borne gastroenteritis – Moderate likelihood: similar symptom profile; contaminated food possible but absence of fever/blood lowers probability.  
3. Irritable bowel syndrome / post-infectious functional diarrhoea – Low-to-moderate: pain relief after stool and anxiety component support, yet acute onset with vomiting less typical.

Quality checks:
● Missing/expected elements: No documented vital signs; no objective temperature; detailed medication list incomplete (inhaler type/dose/frequency unknown); allergy confirmation limited to NKDA; smoking/alcohol history not obtained.  
● Conflicts: Date of birth stated as 1 Jan 1992 (age 31) then corrected to age 48 – conflict noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear overall; minor conversational overlaps but clinically adequate.
